findings.summary: sanitize_label(None) returns None instead of empty string, contradicting the required behavior.
findings.mechanism: The bare `return` on line 198 returns None, not "". Task requires None be treated as an empty string. Any caller of sanitize_label (not just the one export.py call site that pre-guards with `str(... or "")`) that passes None will get None back instead of "", and since the function is typed to return str, downstream code expecting a string (e.g. calling .encode(), len(), or string concatenation) will crash with a TypeError/AttributeError on None.
